thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: prod-api-high-error-rate (sev=P1) — paging sam, priya, lee — see /alerts/prod/api/error-rate

oncall-bot: Context: sudden 5x increase in 500s starting 12:44 UTC; affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. Customer-impact: intermittent request failures and elevated latencies.

Sam (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs and metrics now. Anyone oncall in eu?

Marta (support): Seeing multiple customer tickets noting "partial responses" and timeouts. Top impacted customers: acme-inc (live), merchant-x.

Priya (sre): Thanks. I'm pairing with Sam. Sam — can you confirm if KV cache evictions or OOMs in the runtime?

Sam (oncall): Quick dump: no OOMs on node 7/8, but node 3 showing repeated 429s from internal sequencer. Pushing error sample: ```
ERR 12:45:10 sequencer: request rejected: queue-full
TRACE request_id=abcd1234 route=/v1/generate model=rwkv-13b seq_len=1024
```

Lee (runtime): Queue-full from sequencer implies hot shard or sudden QPS spike. Can we scale the dedicated pool or shift routing? Where's the routing policy?

ops-bot: Autoscaler triggered +2 GPUs to pool-prod-3 at 12:46 UTC. Scaling in-progress (ETA ~60s).

Sam (oncall): Scaling kicked. I'm going to flip routing policy to prefer fallback-variant (quantized) for non-enterprise customers to reduce pressure. Will announce 1-min maintenance to affected customers.

Kate (product): Be careful about quality regressions with quantized fallback. Can we restrict to non-SLA customers and exclude acme-inc?

Sam (oncall): Good call. Excluding acme-inc and merchant-x. Applying policy now: ```
route.policy.set(priority=enterprise_exclude, fallback_model=redwood-quant-v1, predicate=customer_tier!=enterprise)
```

Priya (sre): After routing change, 500s dropped to baseline but latency for some requests increased ~25ms. Autoscaler finished and node pool healthy. Observed a backlog drain window 12:47–12:49.

Ben (eng): Noted several model-serving nodes logged cache eviction floods around 12:44. Hypothesis: a malformed client sent many long-context requests causing KV growth and eviction thrash. We have client_id traces: c12345, c67890.

Marta (support): Those client IDs map to a partner integration rollout — raising an urgent support ticket to pause integration on their side.

Priya (sre): Action items from live mitigation: 1) temporary routing fallback (done); 2) scale-up (done); 3) pause partner traffic (in progress). We should schedule a post-incident review and pull the request traces + KV cache metrics.

Sam (oncall): I'll start the incident timeline and handoff to postmortem. Priya — can you own the RCA? Lee — can you own runtime fix/backport if this is a sequencing hot-spot?

Lee (runtime): I can take the runtime ownership. Initial glance: sequencer queue size spikes when long-context requests exceed configured burst allowance. We should add protective codepaths: early reject for excessive prefix length + better per-client rate limiting.

Kate (product): From product POV, prioritize fixes so enterprise customers (acme-inc) never experience fallback. This is a Sev1 -> Q2 infra priority if RCA confirms model-serving protection gaps.

ops-bot: Incident declared: INC-2026-0452 (created 1784123600). Severity: P1. Impact: partial customer outages for non-enterprise customers and increased error rates for some partners.

Sam (oncall): Handoff: I'm done with live mitigation. Moving to post-incident. Handoff notes: timeline, logs, APM traces attached to the INC.

Priya (sre): Scheduling postmortem: propose 2-hour slot tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Attendees: oncall rotation, runtime, eng, product, support. Kate, confirm?

Kate (product): Confirmed. I'll ensure acme-inc's account team is pre-briefed and excluded from rollout steps.

Ben (eng): Quick note on evidence: I saved sampled traces and KV cache metrics to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0452/artifacts.tar.gz.

Marta (support): Adding customer impact notes to the ticket: severity flags, affected customer list, estimated downtime windows.

Priya (sre): Postmortem agenda draft (for the meeting):
- Timeline + detection
- Root cause hypothesis (sequencer queue + partner long-context flood)
- Mitigations applied & rollback criteria
- Action items, owners, sizing and priority mapping
- Follow-ups: tests and monitoring

Sam (oncall): Creating action items now. I'll seed sizing estimates.

Priya (sre): Please use severity -> priority mapping: P1 incidents -> action items needing SLO target: fix within current quarter if customer-impacting enterprise; otherwise schedule in next quarter with hotfix option.

Sam (oncall): Action item 1: Add early-reject in sequencer for requests with context_length > 2048. Owner: Lee. Estimate: 3 engineer-days. Priority: Q2 H2 (hotfix candidate).

Sam (oncall): Action item 2: Per-client throttling / leaky-bucket enforcement at gateway. Owner: Ben. Estimate: 5 engineer-days. Priority: Q2 (required for partner safety).

Sam (oncall): Action item 3: Improve observability — add KV-cache eviction rate alert and prefix-length histogram to telemetry. Owner: Priya. Estimate: 2 engineer-days. Priority: Q2 (high).

Sam (oncall): Action item 4: Postmortem write-up + customer communication draft. Owner: Kate + Marta. Estimate: 1 engineer-day / 0.5 support-day. Priority: P1 customer comms (today).

Priya (sre): Adding severity-based triage note: If action item touches runtime hot path (Lee's tasks), mark as "critical" and do canary + rollback plan before release. Allocate 1 on-call review day.

Kate (product): Mapping to roadmap: Lee's early-reject is Q2 infra priority (aligns with "reliability: runtime protections" epic). Ben's per-client throttling maps to partner-stability initiative (Q2-Q3). Priya's observability work can be included in the Optimize sprint.

Ben (eng): For sizing: Ben/Lee discuss complexity: sequencer change interacts with request scheduling; 3d estimate becomes 5d if we need cross-language bindings. Let's tentatively mark as 5d until follow-up scoping.

Sam (oncall): OK — updating estimates: sequencer early-reject -> 5 engineer-days (Lee), per-client throttling -> 6 engineer-days (Ben), observability -> 2 engineer-days (Priya), comms -> 1 day (Kate/Marta).

Priya (sre): Creating action items in our tracker:
- INC-2026-0452-A1: sequencer early-reject (owner: Lee, estimate: 5d, priority: critical/Q2)
- INC-2026-0452-A2: gateway per-client throttling (owner: Ben, estimate: 6d, priority: high/Q2)
- INC-2026-0452-A3: KV eviction + prefix histogram (owner: Priya, estimate: 2d, priority: high/Q2)
- INC-2026-0452-A4: postmortem & external comms (owner: Kate/Marta, estimate: 1d, priority: immediate)

Marta (support): I'll start the external comms draft and propose a safe wording for partners.

Kate (product): Let's reserve a canary window and blocked-list for long-context requests until fixes land. We'll add that to the runbook.

ops-bot: Reminder: open incidents with P1 actions must be reviewed at weekly ops meeting. Next meeting: 1784190000.

Sam (oncall): Final note: This mitigation prevented wider customer impact, but partners still saw degraded behavior. Need to tighten partner onboarding controls. Priya/Lee/Ben — please scope a follow-up spike if you need more time for accurate estimates.

Priya (sre): Acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem draft and tag the action items for forced review in 2 days.

Ben (eng): I'll start a spike to evaluate implementation complexity for the per-client rate limiter. ETA for spike: 2 days.

Lee (runtime): Starting work on sequencer early-reject spike; will sync progress in the postmortem doc.

Sam (oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing live page and handing over INC-2026-0452 to the remediation backlog.

oncall-bot: Page closed at 12:58 UTC. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

Priya (sre): Postmortem meeting scheduled and invites sent. See INC-2026-0452 details for artifacts and action items.
